new file mode 100644
index 00000000000..24822181a72
--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/global-secure-access/how-to-configure-home-network-support.md
@@ -0,0 +1,133 @@
+---
+title: Configure home network support for Microsoft Entra Private Access
+description: Learn how to configure home network support so users can access local resources while Microsoft Entra Private Access remains enabled.
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 10/13/2026
+ms.subservice: entra-private-access
+ms.reviewer: katabish
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+# Customer intent: As an administrator, I want to configure home network support so users can access directly connected local resources without disconnecting Microsoft Entra Private Access.
+---
+
+# Configure home network support for Microsoft Entra Private Access (preview)
+
+Home network support in Microsoft Entra Private Access helps users connect to resources on their directly connected local network while Private Access remains enabled. For example, users can connect to a home printer, router, wireless display adapter, or locally hosted virtual machine without disconnecting the Global Secure Access client.
+
+This capability is useful when a Private Access application segment overlaps the user's local subnet. An organization might configure a broad private IP range, such as `10.0.0.0/8` or `192.168.0.0/16`, while a user's home network uses an address within the same range. Without home network support, the Global Secure Access client can acquire traffic intended for the local resource and route it through Private Access, breaking local access.
+
+When **Prefer Local Network** is enabled, the client identifies the directly connected local subnet and sends matching traffic directly to the local network.
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> Home network support is currently in preview. This information relates to a prerelease product that might be substantially modified before release. Microsoft makes no warranties, expressed or implied, with respect to the information provided here. For more information, see the [Microsoft Entra preview terms](https://azure.microsoft.com/support/legal/preview-supplemental-terms/).
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+Before you begin, make sure you have:
+
+- A Microsoft Entra Private Access or Microsoft Entra Suite license.
+- A configured and enabled Private Access traffic forwarding profile.
+- A supported Global Secure Access client with Private Access connected.
+- The [Global Secure Access Administrator](../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#global-secure-access-administrator) role to manage traffic forwarding profiles.
+
+## How home network support works
+
+The Global Secure Access client uses the IP address and subnet mask assigned to a network adapter to calculate the directly connected local subnet.
+
+For example, if an adapter has the address `192.168.4.69/22`, the calculated local subnet is `192.168.4.0/22`. When **Prefer Local Network** is enabled, traffic to a destination in that subnet remains on the local network instead of being acquired by Private Access.
+
+Home network support affects Private Access traffic only. It doesn't bypass Microsoft traffic or internet traffic forwarding policies.
+
+## Enable home network support
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com/) as a Global Secure Access Administrator.
+1. Browse to **Global Secure Access** > **Connect** > **Traffic forwarding**.
+1. Switch to the new v2 experience, if you haven't already.
+1. Open the Private Access traffic forwarding profile that applies to the target users.
+1. Enable the **Allow local subnet bypass** setting.
+1. Save the profile.
+
+:::image type="content" source="media/how-to-configure-home-network-support/allow-local-subnet-bypass.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Private Access traffic forwarding profile Basics page with Allow local subnet bypass enabled.":::
+
+After the updated profile reaches the client, the user can manage the local network preference from the Global Secure Access client.
+
+## Enable Prefer Local Network on the client
+
+1. Open the Global Secure Access client.
+1. Select **Settings**.
+1. Turn on **Prefer Local Network**.
+1. Connect to the local resource again.
+
+:::image type="content" source="media/how-to-configure-home-network-support/prefer-local-network.png" alt-text="Screenshot of Global Secure Access client Settings with Prefer Local Network turned on.":::
+
+The preference remains in effect as the device changes networks. The client calculates the applicable local subnet for the current network connection.
+
+## Understand routing behavior
+
+When **Prefer Local Network** is enabled, routing is evaluated in the following order:
+
+1. Intelligent Local Access, when the configured corporate network detection and application conditions are met.
+1. Home network support for a destination in an eligible directly connected local subnet.
+1. Normal Private Access traffic acquisition and tunneling.
+
+Intelligent Local Access takes precedence so that its authentication requirements can be applied.
+
+### Overlapping corporate and local destinations
+
+A local resource and a corporate private application can use the same IP address or subnet. When **Prefer Local Network** is enabled, a matching destination uses the local path. The corporate resource in the overlapping range isn't reachable through Private Access from that network.
+
+To reach the corporate resource, the user can temporarily turn off **Prefer Local Network**. The client then applies the organization's Private Access forwarding rules.
+
+> [!CAUTION]
+> Enable this capability only for users who need access to local resources. Where possible, avoid configuring corporate applications with address ranges that are likely to overlap users' directly connected home subnets.
+
+## Verify local network routing
+
+Use **Advanced diagnostics** in the Global Secure Access client to verify the routing decision:
+
+1. Open the Global Secure Access client.
+1. Select **Troubleshooting** > **Advanced diagnostics**.
+1. In **Forwarding Profile**, verify that the expected Private Access profile was received.
+1. Open the network traffic view and start collecting traffic.
+1. Connect to the local resource.
+1. Filter the results by the destination IP address.
+1. Verify that the action indicates local bypass.
+
+For more information, see [Global Secure Access client advanced diagnostics](troubleshoot-global-secure-access-client-advanced-diagnostics.md).
+
+## Troubleshoot home network access
+
+### The local resource is still unreachable
+
+- Confirm that **Prefer Local Network** is available and enabled in the client.
+- Confirm that the destination is in the device's directly connected subnet.
+- Confirm that the destination uses an RFC 1918 IPv4 address.
+- In **Advanced diagnostics**, verify that the expected traffic forwarding profile reached the client.
+- Collect traffic while reproducing the issue and review the action for the destination IP address.
+- Verify that the local device and operating-system firewall allow the connection.
+
+### A corporate private application is unreachable
+
+The corporate application's address might overlap the local subnet. Turn off **Prefer Local Network** and try the connection again. If the connection succeeds, the local preference was taking precedence over Private Access for that destination.
+
+Consider publishing the corporate application by FQDN with a more specific application segment or changing the addressing plan to avoid the overlap.
+
+### Prefer Local Network isn't displayed
+
+- Verify that the device runs a supported Global Secure Access client version.
+- Verify that the administrator enabled home network support for the user's Private Access traffic forwarding profile.
+- Verify that the user is assigned to the expected profile.
+- Refresh the client configuration or restart the client after the profile change.
+
+## Limitations
+
+- Home network support applies only to directly connected local subnets. It doesn't provide a general bypass for routed networks behind the local gateway.
+- Only IPv4 private ranges defined by RFC 1918 are supported. IPv6 local subnets aren't supported.
+- Mobile clients aren't supported.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [What is Microsoft Entra Private Access?](concept-private-access.md)
+- [Configure Private Access traffic forwarding](tutorial-private-access-enable-traffic-forwarding.md)
+- [Global Secure Access client overview](concept-clients.md)
+- [Configure Intelligent Local Access](tutorial-private-access-intelligent-local-access.md)
+- [Troubleshoot the Global Secure Access client with Advanced diagnostics](troubleshoot-global-secure-access-client-advanced-diagnostics.md)

englishSummary.headline: Home network support for Microsoft Entra Private Access is documented
englishSummary.summary: A new guide explains how directly connected local resources can remain reachable while Private Access is enabled, including routing behavior, prerequisites, and configuration steps.
englishSummary.adminImpact: Admins can enable Allow local subnet bypass in the applicable Private Access traffic forwarding profile. Users then enable Prefer Local Network in the Global Secure Access client, which helps route overlapping local subnet traffic locally.

+
+## Preapproval and postapproval extensions
+
+Preapproval and postapproval extensions are blocking gates, but they run at different points in the activation workflow.
+
+| Capability | `preApproval` | `postApproval` |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Execution point | Before manual approval | After manual approval and immediately before assignment provisioning |
+| Supported outcomes | `Approved`, `Denied`, `AutoApproved` | `approved`, `denied`, `deferred` |
+| Skip manual approval | Yes, with `AutoApproved` | No, because manual approval is already complete |
+| Deferred evaluation | No | Yes, through `/updateRequest` |
+| Blocks | Manual approval and provisioning | Assignment provisioning |
+| Common scenarios | Compliance prescreening, risk assessment, early denial, and conditional automatic approval | IT service management validation, security scanning, external approval, and asynchronous processing |
+
+Use a preapproval extension to evaluate a request before a PIM approver sees it. Use a postapproval extension when custom logic must run after the built-in PIM approval stage but before PIM provisions the assignment.
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> A postapproval extension doesn't run after role activation. It runs after manual approval, but before the role assignment is provisioned.
+
+### When to use each extension type
+
+Use a preapproval extension to:
+
+- Perform compliance or risk checks before a human approver sees the request.
+- Auto-approve low-risk requests that meet defined criteria.
+- Deny requests early based on external data.
+- Reduce approver workload by filtering clearly valid or invalid requests.
+
+Use a postapproval extension to:
+
+- Run another custom approval workflow after PIM approval.
+- Validate an IT service management ticket before provisioning access.
+- Perform a security scan or another long-running process.
+- Defer the decision and call PIM later with the final outcome.
+
+### Complete a deferred postapproval evaluation
+
+A postapproval extension can return `deferred` when it needs more time to make a decision. PIM places the request in `PostApprovalExtensionPendingEvaluation` and doesn't provision the role assignment. After the asynchronous process finishes, the extension calls `/updateRequest` on the original activation request with a final `approved` or `denied` decision.
+
+The extension must authenticate to the callback API by using the same Microsoft Entra app registration configured for the extension. PIM verifies that the calling application ID matches the registered application. The callback can't return `deferred` again.
+
+The deferred flow works as follows:
+
+1. PIM calls the postapproval extension after manual approval.
+1. The extension returns `deferred` because it needs more time.
+1. PIM moves the request to `PostApprovalExtensionPendingEvaluation`.
+1. The extension completes its asynchronous validation or approval process.
+1. The extension calls the provider-specific `/updateRequest` endpoint with `approved` or `denied`.
+1. PIM validates the callback and either provisions or denies the assignment.
+
+#### Microsoft Entra roles
+
+Use:
+
+```http
+POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignmentScheduleRequests/{requestId}/updateRequest
+Content-Type: application/json
+```
+
+```json
+{
+  "evaluationOutcome": "approved",
+  "evaluationId": "aaaa0000-bb11-2222-33cc-444444dddddd",
+  "reason": "The external compliance system approved the request."
+}
+```
+
+#### PIM for Groups
+
+Use:
+
+```http
+POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/identityGovernance/privilegedAccess/group/assignmentScheduleRequests/{requestId}/updateRequest
+Content-Type: application/json
+```
+
+```json
+{
+  "evaluationOutcome": "denied",
+  "evaluationId": "aaaa0000-bb11-2222-33cc-444444dddddd",
+  "reason": "The external compliance system denied the request."
+}
+```
+
+#### Azure resources
+
+Use:
+
+```http
+POST https://management.azure.com/{scope}/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignmentScheduleRequests/{requestId}/updateRequest?api-version=2020-10-01
+Content-Type: application/json
+```
+
+```json
+{
+  "evaluationOutcome": "denied",
+  "evaluationId": "aaaa0000-bb11-2222-33cc-444444dddddd",
+  "reason": [
+    "The change advisory board rejected ticket CHANGE-9921."
+  ]
+}
+```
+
+#### Callback endpoint summary
+
+| Provider | Endpoint |
+|---|---|
+| Microsoft Entra roles | `POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignmentScheduleRequests/{requestId}/updateRequest` |
+| PIM for Groups | `POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/identityGovernance/privilegedAccess/group/assignmentScheduleRequests/{requestId}/updateRequest` |
+| Azure resources | `POST https://management.azure.com/{scope}/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignmentScheduleRequests/{requestId}/updateRequest?api-version=2020-10-01` |
+
+The callback request body supports the following properties:
+
+| Property | Required | Description |
+|---|---|---|
+| `evaluationOutcome` | Yes | Final outcome. Use `approved` or `denied`; a callback can't return `deferred`. |
+| `evaluationId` | Yes | Correlation identifier from the original extension response. |
+| `reason` | No | Human-readable reason for the decision. Azure Resource Manager accepts a string collection; Microsoft Graph accepts a string. |
+| `scheduleInfo` | No | Microsoft Graph only. Optional updated activation schedule for an approved request. |
+
+Handle callback failures based on the returned HTTP status:
+
+| HTTP status | Cause |
+|---|---|
+| `400 Bad Request` | The request isn't waiting for a callback, or the callback outcome isn't `approved` or `denied`. |
+| `401 Unauthorized` | The calling application doesn't match the app registered for the custom extension. |
+| `404 Not Found` | The request ID doesn't exist. |
+
+## Custom attributes
+
+Custom attributes collect extra key-value context during activation and include it in the extension request. Use custom attributes when your extension needs information that isn't part of the standard request, such as a cost center, project code, business justification category, or identifier in an external system.
+
+Add the attribute names when you create the extension. During activation, the user enters the corresponding values. PIM sends the values in a provider-specific format.
+
+### Azure resources
+
+For Azure resource roles, PIM sends a `customAttributes` array:
+
+```json
+{
+  "customAttributes": [
+    {
+      "attributeName": "costCenter",
+      "attributeValue": "CC-4521"
+    },
+    {
+      "attributeName": "projectCode",
+      "attributeValue": "PROJ-ALPHA"
+    }
+  ]
+}
+```
+
+### Microsoft Entra roles
+
+For Microsoft Entra roles, PIM sends a JSON-encoded `customData` string:
+
+```json
+{
+  "customData": "{\"costCenter\":\"CC-4521\",\"projectCode\":\"PROJ-ALPHA\"}"
+}
+```
+
+### PIM for Groups
+
+For PIM for Groups, PIM also sends a JSON-encoded `customData` string:
+
+```json
+{
+  "customData": "{\"costCenter\":\"CC-4521\",\"approverGroup\":\"finance-approvers\"}"
+}
+```
+
+| Provider | Field | Format |
+|---|---|---|
+| Azure resources | `customAttributes` | Array of `attributeName` and `attributeValue` objects. |
+| Microsoft Entra roles | `customData` | JSON-encoded string. |
+| PIM for Groups | `customData` | JSON-encoded string. |
+
+Validate custom-attribute names and values in your API before using them in a query, workflow, or access decision.
+
+## Quick reference
+
+### Extension type decision matrix
+
+| Scenario | `preApproval` | `postApproval` |
+|---|---|---|
+| Compliance check before approvers | Best fit | Not applicable |
+| Auto-approve low-risk requests | Best fit | Not supported |
+| Block based on external data | Supported | Supported |
+| Custom approval after PIM approval | Not applicable | Best fit |
+| Asynchronous processing with callback | Not supported | Best fit |
+| Security scan before provisioning | Not applicable | Best fit |
+
+### Evaluation outcome quick reference
+
+| Outcome | `preApproval` effect | `postApproval` effect | Callback effect |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| `Approved` / `approved` | Continues to manual approval. | Continues to provisioning. | Resolves a deferred request and provisions the role. |
+| `Denied` / `denied` | Denies the request. | Denies the request. | Resolves a deferred request and denies it. |
+| `deferred` | Not supported. | Pauses and waits for `/updateRequest`. | Not supported; a callback can't defer again. |
+| `AutoApproved` | Skips manual approval. | Not supported. | Not supported. |
+
+### Postapproval request status transitions
+
+The following table shows how the request status transitions based on the postapproval evaluation outcome and the callback decision:
+
+| Stage | Outcome | New status | Next step |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Postapproval extension | `approved` | Granted | PIM provisions the assignment. |
+| Postapproval extension | `denied` | Denied | The request ends. |
+| Postapproval extension | `deferred` | `PostApprovalExtensionPendingEvaluation` | PIM waits for `/updateRequest`. |
+| Callback | `approved` | `PostApprovalExtensionAdminApproved` | PIM provisions the assignment. |
+| Callback | `denied` | `PostApprovalExtensionAdminDenied` | The request ends. |

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Entra: Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO as standalone MFA factors
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Entra will recognize Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO as standalone MFA factors starting early October 2026, allowing users to meet MFA requirements without additional passkeys. No configuration changes are needed, but organizations should update onboarding and MFA registration guidance accordingly.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated October 13, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

What and why

Microsoft Entra will soon recognize Windows Hello for Business (WHfB) and macOS Platform Single Sign-On (PSSO) as standalone multifactor authentication (MFA) factors in supported authentication scenarios.

Today, WHfB and macOS PSSO can satisfy MFA requirements during primary sign-in, but users may still be required to register and use an additional passkey or authentication method for certain step-up authentication prompts, Authentication Strength policies, and sign-in frequency checks.

After this rollout, users who authenticate with WHfB or macOS PSSO will be able to satisfy supported MFA requirements without registering an additional passkey. This change helps organizations expand the use of phishing-resistant authentication methods and reduce reliance on less secure authentication methods. As part of this change, a user's WHfB and macOS PSSO credentials will be displayed in My Security Info as auto-registered passkeys.

Rollout schedule

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): Beginning in early October 2026 and expected to complete in mid-December 2026 (previously late November)

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Entra ID
  • Users who authenticate with Windows Hello for Business
  • Users who authenticate with macOS Platform SSO
  • Organizations using Conditional Access Authentication Strength policies

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra ID
  • Windows Hello for Business
  • macOS Platform SSO
  • Conditional Access
  • Authentication Strength policies

What will happen

After rollout:

  • Users signing in with WHfB or macOS PSSO can complete supported MFA challenges without requiring a separate passkey.
  • WHfB and macOS PSSO will satisfy supported MFA requirements for step-up authentication scenarios.
  • WHfB and macOS PSSO can be used during 2FA to satisfy supported Authentication Strength policy requirements.
  • WHfB and macOS PSSO can be used during 2FA to satisfy supported sign-in frequency challenge requirements.
  • Users whose only MFA method is WHfB or macOS PSSO will be considered MFA-capable.
  • Users who sign in with only a password will no longer be automatically prompted to register an additional MFA method if WHfB or macOS PSSO is their only registered MFA credential.
  • Users with WHfB or macOS PSSO credentials, will be able to see them listed in My Security Info as auto-registered passkeys.

Action required and recommendations

No configuration changes are required.

We recommend reviewing user onboarding and MFA registration processes before rollout. Because WHfB and macOS PSSO credentials are device-bound, users may not be able to complete MFA challenges from devices where those credentials are not available.

Recommended actions:

  • Update onboarding guidance to ensure users register at least one portable MFA method.
  • Consider requiring users to register a synced passkey or Microsoft Authenticator passkey in addition to WHfB or macOS PSSO.
  • Review custom Authentication Strength policies to confirm WHfB and macOS PSSO are allowed where appropriate.
  • Update user documentation because users with only WHfB or macOS PSSO registered will no longer be automatically guided to register an additional MFA method.

Learn more (To be updated closer to GA rollout.)

  • Plan a Windows Hello for Business deployment | Security | Windows | Microsoft Learn
  • Prepare users to provision and use Windows Hello for Business | Security | Windows | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

messageCenterItems.title: Action may be required: Review who can create agents in Microsoft Entra
messageCenterItems.summary: Starting November 4, 2026, default users in Microsoft Entra can create agent blueprints unless administrators disable this via the "Users can create agent blueprints" setting. Admins can restrict this by toggling the setting to No in the Entra admin center before rollout completes in late November.
messageCenterItems.body:
What and why

Microsoft Entra is changing who can create agent blueprints by default. Starting November 4, default users will be able to create new agent blueprints unless an administrator turns off Users can create agent blueprints. This means that users without built-in or custom Entra roles will be able to create new agent blueprints in their organization. From now until rollout begins, you can set your tenant preferences to prepare for this rollout. If you do not want users in your organization to create new agent blueprints and their identities, follow the instructions below. 

Rollout schedule

  • Worldwide: Beginning in early November 2026 and expected to complete by late November 2026

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Entra
  • Default users who don't have a built-in or custom Microsoft Entra role

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra

What will happen

  • Default users will be able to create agent blueprints unless an administrator turns off Users can create agent blueprints. If you set the toggle to No, default users will not be able to create new agents. Supported administrators and users assigned the Agent ID Developer role can continue to create them. 
  • If you change this toggle now, your tenant won't change right away. Your setting takes effect when the rollout begins in early November.

Action required and recommendations

If default users should be allowed to create agents in your organization, no action is required. Choosing to allow users to create agent blueprints will not begin until the functionality is available in your tenant.

To restrict creation:

  1. Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center using this link.
  2. Go to Entra ID > Users > User settings.
  3. Under Default user role permissions, find Users can create agent blueprints.
  4. Set the toggle to No, then save the change.

For more information and instructions on setting the toggle for your organization, see Manage who can create agent blueprints here.

This change affects new agent blueprint creation by default users. It does not:

  • Change or remove existing agent blueprints.
  • Change who can create agent identities from existing blueprints.
  • Block an app or an agent from creating identities
  • Affect creation requirements within platforms such as Microsoft Foundry or Security Copilot, such as requiring licenses and Azure subscriptions.

The new setting is independent of Users can register applications. Review both settings separately.

Learn more

  • Delegate application management administrator permissions - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Entra: Changes to AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager permission for agent identities
messageCenterItems.summary: Starting November 4, Microsoft Entra will stop automatically granting the AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager permission to agent blueprints. Admin consent will be required for agents to create identities. This change, rolling out worldwide in November 2026, enhances control and auditability of agent identity creation.
messageCenterItems.body:
What and why

Microsoft Entra Agent ID is enforcing tighter restrictions for autonomous creation of an agent’s own identities. Currently, all agents are granted AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager upon creation without administrator approval. Starting November 4, Microsoft Entra will no longer automatically grant AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager to agent blueprint principals, and creation of identities will need an admin to grant consent.

Agents that use app-only authentication to create their own agent identities must be explicitly granted the AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager Microsoft Graph application permission or move to another supported authorization model before enforcement reaches their tenant.

Rollout schedule

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in early November 2026 and expected to complete by late November 2026

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Entra 
  • No action is required if your organization doesn't have an agent that depends on the automatic AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager grant.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra

What will happen

Today, an agent blueprint principal is granted AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager automatically. This implicit grant allows the principal to create agent identities without a tenant-admin granting an app-role assignment.

After enforcement, an administrator must grant the Microsoft Graph application permission AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager to agents that needs this authority.

This change:

  • Makes app-only agent identity creation authority visible, auditable, and revocable.
  • Makes AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager revocable if consented
  • Affects existing and future agents.
  • Doesn't remove existing agent identities or agent blueprints.
  • Doesn't remove the ability for agent identity blueprints to create agent identities, when AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager is explicitly granted by an administrator
  • Doesn't affect an agent that uses a directory role to authorize creation of agent identities.

Action required and recommendations

No action is required if your organization doesn't have an agent that depends on the automatic AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager grant.

Identify agents that create agent identities without a signed-in user.

  1. Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center.
  2. Go to Entra ID>Audit Logs.
  3. Set the Category to "ApplicationManagement"
  4. Set the Activity filter to "Add Service Principal"

Find events where the Initiated By (actor) Type is Application and the Target is an agent identity.

For each affected agent:

  1. Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center.
  2. Go to Entra ID>Agent blueprints>Search for your agent blueprint>Granted permissions
  3. Review if the Agent has any other granted permissions that may allow for creation of agent identities. If there are no other permissions allowing for creation, this agent relies on AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager.
  4. Starting October 16, you may grant the explicit AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager Microsoft Graph application permission through tenant-wide admin consent or manual app-role creation. Granting it earlier will cause an error. A successful grant appears in the Granted Permissions table with “An administrator” in the Granted By column.
  5. Test app-only agent identity creation before enforcement begins.
  6. Update operational guidance for a failed request after enforcement.

If an app-only request relies only on the automatic grant after enforcement reaches your tenant, the request will fail with a 403 authorization error.

Learn more

  • For more about how to grant your agents access to resources, visit Grant agents access to Microsoft 365 resources | Microsoft Learn. 
  • For the Microsoft Graph permission reference on AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager, visit Microsoft Graph permissions reference - Microsoft Graph | Microsoft Learn.

Compliance considerations

No specific compliance impacts have been identified for this configuration update.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Entra: Allow password change after secure sign-in with My Sign-Ins
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Entra will enable users to change passwords after secure sign-in using strong credentials (passkey, FIDO2, Windows Hello) without knowing the current password or using SSPR. This feature, disabled by default, requires admin activation and will roll out globally from October to November 2026.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated October 9, 2026: We have updated the content. Thank you for your patience. 

What and Why

We're introducing a new Microsoft Entra capability that allows password change after secure sign-in directly from My Sign-Ins using an existing strong credential, such as a passkey, FIDO2 security key, or Windows Hello for Business. Users can complete this action even if they don't know their current password and without using self-service password reset (SSPR) or contacting the helpdesk.

Many organizations are adopting allowed password changes after secure sign-ins but still maintain passwords for legacy applications and services. This update helps reduce password-related support requests and removes a common barrier to adoption. The feature is disabled by default and requires administrator enablement before users can access it.

Rollout Schedule

  • General Availability (Worldwide and GCC): Beginning end of October 2026 (previously mid-October) and expected to complete by end of November 2026 (previously late October)

Impact on Your Organization

Who is affected

  • Microsoft Entra administrators who manage password change settings
  • Users who have a registered allowed password change after secure sign-in method (passkey, FIDO2 security key, or Windows Hello for Business) and also maintain a password
  • Organizations that choose to enable the feature

Platforms/Services

  • Microsoft Entra
  • My Sign-Ins (mysignins.microsoft.com)

What will happen

  • Because this feature is off by default, there is no change to your users' experience unless you turn it on. 
  • After the feature is enabled, eligible users will see a new Change password option in My Sign-Ins.
  • Users can authenticate set a new password without knowing their existing password.
  • Users are not required to enroll in or use SSPR to complete this action.
  • Administrators can choose to enable or disable the capability through Microsoft Entra management interfaces available at release.
  • Authentication continues to require a strong password change method, such as a passkey, FIDO2 security key, or Windows Hello for Business.
  • The setting is tenant-wide: you can turn it on for your entire tenant or leave it off for everyone. There is no per-user or per-group scoping. 

Action Required/Recommendations

No action is required.

If your organization plans to support allowed password changes after secure sign-in:

  • Review your password management and allowed password changes after secure sign-in strategy.
  • Evaluate whether enabling this capability aligns with your organization's security and support requirements.
  • Communicate the new self-service capability to helpdesk and support teams.
  • Update internal user guidance and documentation as needed.
  • If your organization chooses to offer allowed password changes after secure sign-in, enable the feature through the Microsoft Entra admin experience or supported APIs when it becomes available in October 2026.

Learn more 

  • Microsoft Learn documentation will be available when the feature releases in October. 

Compliance Considerations

QuestionAnswer
Does the change include an admin control?Yes. The feature is disabled by default and requires explicit administrator enablement.
Does the change modify how users can access or correct their personal data?Yes. Users gain a new self-service method to update their password using an existing allowed password change after secure sign-in.

groups.summary: The documentation now specifies tenant ID or the tenant’s onmicrosoft.com domain for the issuer URI, says custom verified domains aren’t supported, and requires matching onmicrosoft.com values for domain_hint. groups.title: id-governance
groups.summary: The documentation adds postapproval extensions with deferred outcomes and asynchronous validation before assignment provisioning. It also describes collecting attributes such as cost center and project code, along with the required Graph permissions and endpoint configuration.

groups.summary: Step 1 now links to the permissions reference anchor without the `.md` suffix.
